## EIDL in Iowa [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/iowa.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

EIDL in Iowa [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Iowa residents.

EIDL Landscape in Iowa

Moderate EIDL volume; rural/small-town small businesses relied heavily.

COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) were issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration under 15 U.S.C. Section 636(b)(2) as amended by the CARES Act. For Iowa businesses, EIDLs went up to $2 million per borrower, at 3.75% interest for for-profits and 2.75% for nonprofits, over 30-year terms. The first-year deferment and 24-month extension kept most Iowa borrowers out of default until 2023-2024.

Is EIDL Forgivable?

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

The main loan portion must be repaid. Iowa small-business owners facing EIDL default have several paths:

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

UCC Liens on Your Iowa Business

Collateral structure: IA Article 9 UCC; Iowa homestead exemption unlimited for primary residence.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All equipment, furniture, fixtures, machinery.

All accounts receivable and contract rights.

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

For a Iowa small business planning asset sale, ownership transfer, or bankruptcy, the UCC-1 must be addressed. Failure to clear the lien before sale can trigger SBA recapture rights.

Personal Guarantee Exposure in Iowa

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in Iowa means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

Subchapter V and EIDL in Iowa

Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (11 U.S.C. Sections 1181-1195) is the small-business restructuring track enacted by the Small Business Reorganization Act of 2019. For Iowa EIDL borrowers, Subchapter V offers:

Automatic stay. SBA collection halts on filing under 11 U.S.C. Section 362.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most Iowa EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in Iowa

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For Iowa borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

Iowa Small Business Chapter 7 vs Sub V Decision

For Iowa EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

FactorChapter 7 (business)Subchapter V

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

Iowa Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

Iowa-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

## EIDL in Maine [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/maine.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

EIDL in Maine [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Maine residents.

EIDL Landscape in Maine

Moderate EIDL volume; tourism + fishing small businesses.

COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) were issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration under 15 U.S.C. Section 636(b)(2) as amended by the CARES Act. For Maine businesses, EIDLs went up to $2 million per borrower, at 3.75% interest for for-profits and 2.75% for nonprofits, over 30-year terms. The first-year deferment and 24-month extension kept most Maine borrowers out of default until 2023-2024.

Is EIDL Forgivable?

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

The main loan portion must be repaid. Maine small-business owners facing EIDL default have several paths:

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

UCC Liens on Your Maine Business

Collateral structure: ME Article 9 UCC.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All equipment, furniture, fixtures, machinery.

All accounts receivable and contract rights.

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

For a Maine small business planning asset sale, ownership transfer, or bankruptcy, the UCC-1 must be addressed. Failure to clear the lien before sale can trigger SBA recapture rights.

Personal Guarantee Exposure in Maine

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in Maine means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

Subchapter V and EIDL in Maine

Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (11 U.S.C. Sections 1181-1195) is the small-business restructuring track enacted by the Small Business Reorganization Act of 2019. For Maine EIDL borrowers, Subchapter V offers:

Automatic stay. SBA collection halts on filing under 11 U.S.C. Section 362.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most Maine EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in Maine

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For Maine borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

Maine Small Business Chapter 7 vs Sub V Decision

For Maine EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

FactorChapter 7 (business)Subchapter V

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

Maine Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

Maine-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

Related Maine Resources

Forgiveness (grant advance only)

SBA Offer in Compromise

Hardship options

Bankruptcy and EIDL

EIDL loan structure

Advance vs loan

## EIDL in Michigan [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/michigan.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Michigan residents.

## EIDL in Minnesota [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/minnesota.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

EIDL in Minnesota [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Minnesota residents.

EIDL Landscape in Minnesota

High EIDL; Twin Cities metro concentration.

COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) were issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration under 15 U.S.C. Section 636(b)(2) as amended by the CARES Act. For Minnesota businesses, EIDLs went up to $2 million per borrower, at 3.75% interest for for-profits and 2.75% for nonprofits, over 30-year terms. The first-year deferment and 24-month extension kept most Minnesota borrowers out of default until 2023-2024.

Is EIDL Forgivable?

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

The main loan portion must be repaid. Minnesota small-business owners facing EIDL default have several paths:

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

UCC Liens on Your Minnesota Business

Collateral structure: MN Article 9 UCC.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All equipment, furniture, fixtures, machinery.

All accounts receivable and contract rights.

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

For a Minnesota small business planning asset sale, ownership transfer, or bankruptcy, the UCC-1 must be addressed. Failure to clear the lien before sale can trigger SBA recapture rights.

Personal Guarantee Exposure in Minnesota

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in Minnesota means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

Minnesota Federal Bankruptcy Data

When EIDL collection pressure outpaces business cash flow, small-business owners in Minnesota often file bankruptcy - either personal Ch 7/13 for PG exposure or business Ch 11/Sub V. These FJC numbers show the Minnesota filing environment.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 395 bankruptcy cases from Minnesota's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 737999.7%0.3%

Chapter 1316n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Subchapter V and EIDL in Minnesota

Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (11 U.S.C. Sections 1181-1195) is the small-business restructuring track enacted by the Small Business Reorganization Act of 2019. For Minnesota EIDL borrowers, Subchapter V offers:

Automatic stay. SBA collection halts on filing under 11 U.S.C. Section 362.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most Minnesota EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in Minnesota

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For Minnesota borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

Minnesota Small Business Chapter 7 vs Sub V Decision

For Minnesota EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

FactorChapter 7 (business)Subchapter V

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

Minnesota Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

Minnesota-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

Related Minnesota Resources

## EIDL in Montana [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/montana.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Nebraska residents.

Moderate EIDL volume.

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

The main loan portion must be repaid. Nebraska small-business owners facing EIDL default have several paths:

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

UCC Liens on Your Nebraska Business

Collateral structure: NE Article 9 UCC.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All equipment, furniture, fixtures, machinery.

All accounts receivable and contract rights.

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

For a Nebraska small business planning asset sale, ownership transfer, or bankruptcy, the UCC-1 must be addressed. Failure to clear the lien before sale can trigger SBA recapture rights.

Personal Guarantee Exposure in Nebraska

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in Nebraska means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

Nebraska Federal Bankruptcy Data

When EIDL collection pressure outpaces business cash flow, small-business owners in Nebraska often file bankruptcy - either personal Ch 7/13 for PG exposure or business Ch 11/Sub V. These FJC numbers show the Nebraska filing environment.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 84 bankruptcy cases from Nebraska's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 757100.0%0.0%

Chapter 119n/an/a

Chapter 1318n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Subchapter V and EIDL in Nebraska

Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (11 U.S.C. Sections 1181-1195) is the small-business restructuring track enacted by the Small Business Reorganization Act of 2019. For Nebraska EIDL borrowers, Subchapter V offers:

Automatic stay. SBA collection halts on filing under 11 U.S.C. Section 362.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most Nebraska EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in Nebraska

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For Nebraska borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

Nebraska Small Business Chapter 7 vs Sub V Decision

For Nebraska EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

FactorChapter 7 (business)Subchapter V

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

Nebraska Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

Nebraska-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

## EIDL in Nevada [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/nevada.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

EIDL in Nevada [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Nevada residents.

EIDL Landscape in Nevada

Very high EIDL volume per capita; Las Vegas hospitality near-total shutdown in 2020-21 drove maximum draw.

COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) were issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration under 15 U.S.C. Section 636(b)(2) as amended by the CARES Act. For Nevada businesses, EIDLs went up to $2 million per borrower, at 3.75% interest for for-profits and 2.75% for nonprofits, over 30-year terms. The first-year deferment and 24-month extension kept most Nevada borrowers out of default until 2023-2024.

Is EIDL Forgivable?

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

UCC Liens on Your New Mexico Business

Collateral structure: NM Article 9 UCC.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All equipment, furniture, fixtures, machinery.

All accounts receivable and contract rights.

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

For a New Mexico small business planning asset sale, ownership transfer, or bankruptcy, the UCC-1 must be addressed. Failure to clear the lien before sale can trigger SBA recapture rights.

Personal Guarantee Exposure in New Mexico

PG rules: PG over $200K; NM community-property exposure for spouse.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in New Mexico means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

Subchapter V and EIDL in New Mexico

Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (11 U.S.C. Sections 1181-1195) is the small-business restructuring track enacted by the Small Business Reorganization Act of 2019. For New Mexico EIDL borrowers, Subchapter V offers:

Automatic stay. SBA collection halts on filing under 11 U.S.C. Section 362.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most New Mexico EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in New Mexico

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For New Mexico borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

New Mexico Small Business Chapter 7 vs Sub V Decision

For New Mexico EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

FactorChapter 7 (business)Subchapter V

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

New Mexico Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

New Mexico-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

## EIDL in New York [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/new-york.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

EIDL in New York [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for New York residents.

EIDL Landscape in New York

Very high EIDL volume; NYC small-business density produced massive aggregate draw.

COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) were issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration under 15 U.S.C. Section 636(b)(2) as amended by the CARES Act. For New York businesses, EIDLs went up to $2 million per borrower, at 3.75% interest for for-profits and 2.75% for nonprofits, over 30-year terms. The first-year deferment and 24-month extension kept most New York borrowers out of default until 2023-2024.

Is EIDL Forgivable?

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

The main loan portion must be repaid. New York small-business owners facing EIDL default have several paths:

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

Collateral structure: NY Article 9 UCC.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in New York means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

New York Federal Bankruptcy Data

When EIDL collection pressure outpaces business cash flow, small-business owners in New York often file bankruptcy - either personal Ch 7/13 for PG exposure or business Ch 11/Sub V. These FJC numbers show the New York filing environment.

Subchapter V and EIDL in New York

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most New York EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in New York

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For New York borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in Ohio means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

Ohio Federal Bankruptcy Data

When EIDL collection pressure outpaces business cash flow, small-business owners in Ohio often file bankruptcy - either personal Ch 7/13 for PG exposure or business Ch 11/Sub V. These FJC numbers show the Ohio filing environment.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 4,120 bankruptcy cases from Ohio's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 73,53597.7%1.8%

Chapter 11149n/an/a

Chapter 1343651.1%48.9%

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Subchapter V and EIDL in Ohio

Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (11 U.S.C. Sections 1181-1195) is the small-business restructuring track enacted by the Small Business Reorganization Act of 2019. For Ohio EIDL borrowers, Subchapter V offers:

Automatic stay. SBA collection halts on filing under 11 U.S.C. Section 362.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most Ohio EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in Ohio

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For Ohio borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

Ohio Small Business Chapter 7 vs Sub V Decision

For Ohio EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

FactorChapter 7 (business)Subchapter V

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

Ohio Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

Ohio-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

## EIDL in Oklahoma [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/oklahoma.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

EIDL in Oklahoma [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Oklahoma residents.

EIDL Landscape in Oklahoma

Moderate-high EIDL; OKC and Tulsa metros concentrated.

COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) were issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration under 15 U.S.C. Section 636(b)(2) as amended by the CARES Act. For Oklahoma businesses, EIDLs went up to $2 million per borrower, at 3.75% interest for for-profits and 2.75% for nonprofits, over 30-year terms. The first-year deferment and 24-month extension kept most Oklahoma borrowers out of default until 2023-2024.

Is EIDL Forgivable?

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

The main loan portion must be repaid. Oklahoma small-business owners facing EIDL default have several paths:

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

UCC Liens on Your Oklahoma Business

Collateral structure: OK Article 9 UCC; OK unlimited homestead protects primary residence.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All equipment, furniture, fixtures, machinery.

All accounts receivable and contract rights.

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

For a Oklahoma small business planning asset sale, ownership transfer, or bankruptcy, the UCC-1 must be addressed. Failure to clear the lien before sale can trigger SBA recapture rights.

Personal Guarantee Exposure in Oklahoma

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in Oklahoma means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

Oklahoma Federal Bankruptcy Data

When EIDL collection pressure outpaces business cash flow, small-business owners in Oklahoma often file bankruptcy - either personal Ch 7/13 for PG exposure or business Ch 11/Sub V. These FJC numbers show the Oklahoma filing environment.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 112 bankruptcy cases from Oklahoma's federal bankruptcy courts.

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

Subchapter V and EIDL in Rhode Island

Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (11 U.S.C. Sections 1181-1195) is the small-business restructuring track enacted by the Small Business Reorganization Act of 2019. For Rhode Island EIDL borrowers, Subchapter V offers:

Automatic stay. SBA collection halts on filing under 11 U.S.C. Section 362.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most Rhode Island EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in Rhode Island

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For Rhode Island borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

Rhode Island Small Business Chapter 7 vs Sub V Decision

For Rhode Island EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

FactorChapter 7 (business)Subchapter V

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

Rhode Island Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

Rhode Island-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

## EIDL in South Carolina [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/south-carolina.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

EIDL in South Carolina [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for South Carolina residents.

EIDL Landscape in South Carolina

Moderate-high EIDL; coastal tourism concentration.

COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) were issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration under 15 U.S.C. Section 636(b)(2) as amended by the CARES Act. For South Carolina businesses, EIDLs went up to $2 million per borrower, at 3.75% interest for for-profits and 2.75% for nonprofits, over 30-year terms. The first-year deferment and 24-month extension kept most South Carolina borrowers out of default until 2023-2024.

Is EIDL Forgivable?

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

The main loan portion must be repaid. South Carolina small-business owners facing EIDL default have several paths:

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

UCC Liens on Your South Carolina Business

Collateral structure: SC Article 9 UCC.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All equipment, furniture, fixtures, machinery.

All accounts receivable and contract rights.

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

For a South Carolina small business planning asset sale, ownership transfer, or bankruptcy, the UCC-1 must be addressed. Failure to clear the lien before sale can trigger SBA recapture rights.

Personal Guarantee Exposure in South Carolina

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in South Carolina means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

South Carolina Federal Bankruptcy Data

When EIDL collection pressure outpaces business cash flow, small-business owners in South Carolina often file bankruptcy - either personal Ch 7/13 for PG exposure or business Ch 11/Sub V. These FJC numbers show the South Carolina filing environment.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 772 bankruptcy cases from South Carolina's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 7301n/an/a

Chapter 11137n/an/a

Chapter 13334n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most Texas EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in Texas

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For Texas borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

Texas Small Business Chapter 7 vs Sub V Decision

For Texas EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

FactorChapter 7 (business)Subchapter V

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

Texas Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

Texas-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

## EIDL in Utah [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/utah.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

EIDL in Utah [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for Utah residents.

EIDL Landscape in Utah

Moderate-high EIDL; Wasatch Front concentration.

COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) were issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration under 15 U.S.C. Section 636(b)(2) as amended by the CARES Act. For Utah businesses, EIDLs went up to $2 million per borrower, at 3.75% interest for for-profits and 2.75% for nonprofits, over 30-year terms. The first-year deferment and 24-month extension kept most Utah borrowers out of default until 2023-2024.

Is EIDL Forgivable?

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

The main loan portion must be repaid. Utah small-business owners facing EIDL default have several paths:

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

UCC Liens on Your Utah Business

Collateral structure: UT Article 9 UCC.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All equipment, furniture, fixtures, machinery.

All accounts receivable and contract rights.

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

For a Utah small business planning asset sale, ownership transfer, or bankruptcy, the UCC-1 must be addressed. Failure to clear the lien before sale can trigger SBA recapture rights.

Personal Guarantee Exposure in Utah

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in Utah means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

Subchapter V and EIDL in Utah

Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (11 U.S.C. Sections 1181-1195) is the small-business restructuring track enacted by the Small Business Reorganization Act of 2019. For Utah EIDL borrowers, Subchapter V offers:

Automatic stay. SBA collection halts on filing under 11 U.S.C. Section 362.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most Utah EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in Utah

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For Utah borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

For Utah EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

Utah Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

Utah-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

Washington Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

Washington-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.

## EIDL in West Virginia [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee
Source: https://eidlloanforgiveness.com/states/west-virginia.html

← eidlloanforgiveness.com home

EIDL in West Virginia [2026]: Forgiveness, UCC Liens, Bankruptcy, and Personal Guarantee

State-specific rules, federal court data, and practical guidance for West Virginia residents.

EIDL Landscape in West Virginia

Moderate EIDL volume.

COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) were issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration under 15 U.S.C. Section 636(b)(2) as amended by the CARES Act. For West Virginia businesses, EIDLs went up to $2 million per borrower, at 3.75% interest for for-profits and 2.75% for nonprofits, over 30-year terms. The first-year deferment and 24-month extension kept most West Virginia borrowers out of default until 2023-2024.

Is EIDL Forgivable?

The main COVID EIDL loan is NOT forgivable. This is the single most common confusion. Only the EIDL Advance (the $1,000-$10,000 grant piece) was forgivable, and the Targeted EIDL Advance and Supplemental Targeted Advance for qualifying businesses in low-income communities.

The main loan portion must be repaid. West Virginia small-business owners facing EIDL default have several paths:

SBA Offer in Compromise (OIC) - negotiate a reduced payoff based on business closure, asset depletion, or collection difficulty. See SBA OIC mechanics.

Hardship Accommodation Plan (HAP) - reduced payment for 6-12 months, renewable.

Treasury Offset - If the loan is transferred to Treasury for collection, tax refunds and federal payments are offset.

Bankruptcy - Chapter 7, Subchapter V, or personal Chapter 7/13 depending on structure.

See what is and is not forgivable and hardship options.

UCC Liens on Your West Virginia Business

Collateral structure: WV Article 9 UCC.

For EIDL loans over $25,000 (originally $200,000 pre-September 2020 modification), the SBA filed a UCC-1 financing statement against the borrowing entity's business assets. This blanket lien typically covers:

All equipment, furniture, fixtures, machinery.

All accounts receivable and contract rights.

All inventory.

All general intangibles (goodwill, IP, licenses).

Proceeds of any of the above.

For a West Virginia small business planning asset sale, ownership transfer, or bankruptcy, the UCC-1 must be addressed. Failure to clear the lien before sale can trigger SBA recapture rights.

Personal Guarantee Exposure in West Virginia

PG rules: PG over $200K.

EIDL loans above $200,000 required a personal guarantee from owners with 20%+ equity. When the business defaults, the SBA (or Treasury after referral) can pursue the PG signer personally - even if the business is dissolved. PG exposure in West Virginia means:

Treasury Offset Program (TOP) intercepts federal payments (tax refunds, SSA in excess of $750/month, federal contractor payments).

Administrative wage garnishment under 31 U.S.C. Section 3720D (up to 15% of disposable pay).

Credit-report reporting as defaulted federal debt.

Potential DOJ referral for judgment suit if amounts and collectability warrant.

West Virginia Federal Bankruptcy Data

When EIDL collection pressure outpaces business cash flow, small-business owners in West Virginia often file bankruptcy - either personal Ch 7/13 for PG exposure or business Ch 11/Sub V. These FJC numbers show the West Virginia filing environment.

Numbers below are from the Federal Judicial Center Integrated Database covering 61 bankruptcy cases from West Virginia's federal bankruptcy courts.

ChapterCasesDischarge RateDismissal Rate

Chapter 75498.1%1.9%

Chapter 111n/an/a

Chapter 136n/an/a

Rates computed on resolved cases only. Source: FJC Integrated Database.

Subchapter V and EIDL in West Virginia

Subchapter V of Chapter 11 (11 U.S.C. Sections 1181-1195) is the small-business restructuring track enacted by the Small Business Reorganization Act of 2019. For West Virginia EIDL borrowers, Subchapter V offers:

Automatic stay. SBA collection halts on filing under 11 U.S.C. Section 362.

No disclosure statement required. Simplifies the plan confirmation timeline - typically 90 days from filing.

No competing plan. Only the debtor proposes a plan; avoids creditor-plan leverage.

Cramdown simplified. Plan can be confirmed over creditor objection if it satisfies "fair and equitable" test, which is more debtor-friendly than standard Chapter 11.

Projected disposable income (PDI) commitment. 3-5 year plan commits PDI rather than full face-value repayment.

Debt cap. $3,424,000 aggregate noncontingent liquidated debt (2025 adjusted figure; increases with CPI). Most West Virginia EIDL-only small businesses fit within the cap.

Subchapter V trustee is a non-operating oversight figure; the debtor remains in possession.

Bankruptcy Discharge of EIDL in West Virginia

EIDL is not among the nondischargeable debts listed in 11 U.S.C. Section 523(a). For West Virginia borrowers, this means:

Business-only EIDL (no PG) - In a business Ch 7, the loan is discharged with the entity's dissolution. No personal exposure because there was no PG.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 7 - The PG liability is discharged unless the SBA can prove 523(a)(2) fraud, 523(a)(4) fiduciary misconduct, or 523(a)(6) willful-malicious injury - rare in commercial lending contexts.

PG'd EIDL, personal Ch 13 - PG liability is paid pro-rata through the plan; unpaid balance discharged at plan completion.

Business Ch 11 / Sub V - EIDL treated as secured to the value of collateral, unsecured for the balance. Unsecured portion gets plan treatment.

The SBA does periodically challenge discharge on 523(a)(2) grounds when it can show the borrower materially misrepresented business conditions or mis-used loan proceeds. Document retention of original application, use-of-proceeds records, and communications is critical.

West Virginia Small Business Chapter 7 vs Sub V Decision

For West Virginia EIDL borrowers weighing Ch 7 vs Sub V:

FactorChapter 7 (business)Subchapter V

Business continues?No - liquidationYes - reorganization

CostLower (trustee handles)Higher (debtor-in-possession)

Timeline~4-6 months~6-12 months to confirmation; 3-5 year plan

PG exposureSeparate personal filing often neededPlan can address jointly via companion personal filing

EIDL lien on assetsTrustee disposes of collateralDebtor retains operational assets under plan

See bankruptcy and EIDL deep-dive.

West Virginia Treasury Offset and EIDL Collection

When SBA transfers a defaulted EIDL to Treasury for collection (typically 120-180 days after default), the full Treasury Offset Program toolkit activates: federal tax refund intercepts, SSA above the $750/month floor, federal contract payment intercepts, and administrative wage garnishment up to 15% of disposable pay. See Treasury Offset mechanics.

West Virginia-specific: state tax refunds are not subject to federal TOP. Only federal payments. State-law exemptions (homestead, ERISA retirement) are respected by federal collection for account-level seizures, but do not block wage garnishment or tax-refund offsets.
